newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CAPITALS FIRE HEAD COACH SCHOENFELD.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CAPITALS FIRE HEAD COACH SCHOENFELD.

text.p: The Washington Capitals continued their housecleaning Tuesday by firing head coach Jim Schoenfeld, who failed to take his team to the playoffs this spring and won just one playoff series in 3 1/2 seasons on the job.
Capitals chairman Abe Pollin dismissed general manager David Poile last month.
"I believe Jim did an admirable job coaching this team, especially through a difficult injury situation," said Pollin.
"But with a change in the general manager's position, I felt that Jim should be given an opportunity to pursue other interests outside of the Captials orgainzation."
Schoenfeld leaves Washington with a 113-102-34 record.

This season, Poile traded away youth in goaltender Jim Carey and forwards Jason Allison and Anson Carter to acquire centre Adam Oates, right wing Rick Tocchet and goaltender Bill Ranford from the Boston Bruins.
But instead of peaking and making the playoffs, Washington was left out of the postseason with a 33-40-9 record.
The Capitals won a first-round playoff series from Pittsburgh in 1994, but were eliminated by Pittsburgh in the opening round in each of the next two seasons.
Schoenfeld also was a head coach at Buffalo and New Jersey. His best year was 1988, when he took New Jersey to within one game of the Stanley Cup Finals.
Schoenfeld played 13 seasons in the NHL as a defenceman with Buffalo, Detroit and Boston.
The Capitals become the sixth team to dismiss their head coach since the end of the regular season, joining Anaheim, Boston, Montreal, Phoenix and San Jose.
